title: Power annihilation of the cokernel of a kernel-restricted pullback projection
statement: Let X be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], J a quasi-coherent ideal, and F,Fprime,H,G arbitrary O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Products by ideal powers use [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk], and formal quotients use [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Let a:F→H, aprime:Fprime→H, s≥1, and assume J^s coker(aprime)=0. For n≥0 and any morphism d:F×_H Fprime→G/J^(n+1)G, let f:ker(d)→F be the kernel inclusion followed by first projection. Then J^(s+n+1)coker(f)=0. No coherence, Noetherianity, formal compatibility or kernel-torsion assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0889(1), comparison away from the closed subset; Tag 0CYV(2), product-annihilator argument

proof.text: The pullback square induces a monomorphism coker(P→F)→coker(aprime): the class of x maps to the class of a(x); if that class is zero, a(x)=aprime(y), and (x,y) in P kills the original class. The coimage monomorphism identifies coker(ker(d)→P) with a subobject of the target quotient.

Use the composition case of the snake lemma, realized by Mathlib kernelCokernelCompSequence_exact, to obtain the exact cokernel complex coker(ker(d)→P)→coker(ker(d)→F)→coker(P→F). Pass exactness and the two monomorphisms to module stalks. At each use, obtain stalk injectivity directly from the public module_stalk_exact sectionwise-monomorphism clause and Mathlib ModuleCat.mono_iff_injective, using evaluation.map_mono; no duplicate stalk-injectivity helper is stated.

The ideal-product and quotient stalk formulas show that the first outer term is killed by I^(n+1), and the last one by I^s. For b in the middle stalk and t in I^s, its image satisfies g(tb)=0, so exactness gives tb=f(z). For r in I^(n+1), rtb=f(rz)=0. Thus I^(n+1)I^s kills the middle stalk.

Use I^(n+1)I^s=I^(s+n+1), the injective ideal-product stalk inclusion and the zero-stalk criterion for sheaves (Mathlib TopCat.Sheaf.isZero_iff_stalkFunctor_obj_isZero). The forgetful functors are faithful and preserve zero maps, so the sheaf ideal product is zero.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteKernelPullback_cokernel_annihilated
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    {F F' H G : X.Modules} (a : F ⟶ H) (a' : F' ⟶ H)
    (s : ℕ) (hs : 1 ≤ s)
    (hc : IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
      (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι s).2 (cokernel a')))
    (n : ℕ) (d : pullback a a' ⟶ formalModuleQuotient J (n + 1) G) :
    IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct
      (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι (s + n + 1)).2
        (cokernel (kernel.ι d ≫ pullback.fst a a')))
